messages:
maya: Quick sync — need a decision on sequencing for Q3. We have product's fast-cache feature (big conversion win) vs infra SLO cleanup (KV eviction/compaction). Both touch tail latency, ops toil, and cost. Can we do a 10-min call or decide async?

devin: product: fast-cache increases auth conversion ~12% for paying users. RICE quick calc: Reach ~200k/day, Impact 8, Confidence 0.6, Effort 3 -> score ~320. Want to ship end of month.

sasha: infra: the feature increases sustained reqs ~18% and keeps hotter KV working set. Our current p99 headroom is small. Infra work estimate: ~6w eng + 2w rollout + oncall support. Risk: p99 regression and extra toil during ramp.

riley: oncall: last KV incident caused 3 pages in 24h; we've been firefighting compaction. Toil to stabilize if we ship without prep: ~15 hrs/week for ~6 weeks. Shipping first without infra prep will likely add pages.

devin: we can throttle the rollout to 50% for the first week to reduce ramp.

sasha: throttling helps but doesn't eliminate sustained pressure. My proposal: a tight SRE timebox (2 weeks, but minimal "acceptance" work can be ~6 business days) to add eviction metrics/alerts, a small rate-limiter, and a perf test before canary. That should cut expected oncall toil ~50%.

maya: Product needs a firm tradeoff. What's the minimal SRE safety work to accept the feature at 50% flag? What's rollback plan?

sasha: Minimal actionable list: add KV eviction metric + alert (1d), implement simple rate-limit gating on the fast-cache path (2d), run a perf suite with traffic shape (3d). Total ~6 business days. Rollback = flip feature flag + autoscale policy. Note: autoscale helps throughput but not tail latency if KV hot spots remain.

devin: OK. If we delay 6d for safety, estimated conversion loss is ~1.5% — still net positive if we avoid a page storm.

riley: Proposed sequencing: 1) SRE minimal prep (6d) 2) deploy a 10% canary with guardrails: p99 < 350ms and error rate < 0.15% over 5m windows. If guardrail trips for 3 consecutive windows, auto rollback. Ops will monitor.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary created on prod-canary-3 at 2098765400. Logs: https://logs/redwood/abc (streaming).

maya: Decision: do the 6 business days of SRE prep, then a 10% canary with the guardrails above. Devin to update rollout plan and conversion modeling, Sasha + Riley own alerts/runbooks. I'll tag fast-cache in the roadmap as "ready-next" with label "requires-sre-prep".

devin: ack :thumbsup:

sasha: opening tickets now and will schedule the spike into the next sprint (assigning 2 engineers).

riley: I'll author a short 1-pager runbook and paging scenario and put it in the incident playbooks.

maya: Thanks all — I’ll record notes + add a quick RICE delta in the roadmap doc so PMs can see the gating decision.
